rows.claim: Deployment holds build, params, bound, floor, algorithm, budgets, Schedule, warnings
rows.fix: Add the `Lattice` (the loop's index-to-time map, §10.5) to the list of what the `Deployment` holds, before the `Schedule`.
rows.note: The struct has a thirteenth field `lattice` (D-445) that the list omits; probe:58 prints the field names.

rows.claim: If any unanchored component exists, deployment must declare Δt_base
rows.fix: **`Δt_base = :derive` is refused if any unanchored component exists** ([D-283][d-283], [D-443][d-443]). The refusal is constructive, carrying the suggestion message of the grid diagnostics.
rows.note: D-443 made Δt_base default to Δt_frame, so no declaration is required. Only :derive is refused (:unanchored). Deployment(MultiRate; Δt_frame = 1//100) binds with no Δt_base.

rows.claim: an algorithm the stepper seam does not know is refused
rows.fix: Collect an `AbstractAlgorithm` with no `proposes` method as `DeploymentInvalid` on `algorithm`, or narrow the sentence to an algorithm that is not an `AbstractAlgorithm`.
rows.note: Only a non-AbstractAlgorithm is refused (:range). A user subtype with no proposes method escapes as a raw MethodError from proposes (deployment.jl:570), shown by the probe.

rows.claim: framework methods cover three kinds of type: Real, Bool, enums
rows.fix: Framework methods cover four kinds of type: `Real`, with `zero(T)`; `Bool`, with `false`; enums, with their first instance; and `StaticArray`, with `zero(P)`.
rows.note: declare.jl:935 defines probe_value(::Type{P}) where P<:StaticArray = zero(P), a fourth arm. D-051 lists zero, false, first instance and T(), and no entry records the fourth. probe:452 shows an SVector gives [0.0, 0.0].

rows.claim: abstract entries only occur on component-fed inputs
rows.fix: Abstract entries occur on component-fed inputs and, beside a concrete co-consumer, on a root input, where the concrete consumer fixes the type. With no concrete consumer the root input is `AbstractAtRoot`.
rows.note: A root input with one concrete and one abstract consumer builds: the abstract co-consumer is checked against the concrete type (build.jl:925-930). Synthesis still sees only the concrete type.

rows.claim: everything the probe writes is garbage once the build finishes
rows.fix: Probe values never serve as initial root-input values: the executor seeds cells with them only until a writer replaces them, and `init!` refuses a root input no condition covers ([§14.6]).
rows.note: compile seeds each component product and each root-input cell with the probe value (build.jl:1507-1516), and a frozen discrete cell keeps its probe product. The build output is not garbage.
